_disclaimer: This data is manually curated. Verify fees and procedures at the specific court registry before filing.

documents_required: Copies of documents to be relied upon
regular_civil_suit.court_fees_formula: Based on suit value: 1% of amount up to ₹15,000, then graduated scale up to ₹30 lakhs
regular_civil_suit.limitation_period: 3 years from when cause of action arises
regular_civil_suit.limitation_calculation: From date of breach/contract/demand, depending on nature of suit
steps: Draft and file plaint with court fee
regular_civil_suit.punjab_specific_notes: District courts follow Punjab Civil Courts Act. Filing through eCourts portal mandatory in most districts.

documents_required: Court fee stamps (same as regular suit)
summary_suit.court_fees_formula: Same as regular civil suit based on claim amount
summary_suit.limitation_calculation: From date debt became due or contract breached
steps: File summary suit with evidence on affidavit
Court may grant leave to defend or pass judgment
If leave granted, matter proceeds as regular suit
If no leave, judgment passed immediately
summary_suit.typical_timeline: 6-12 months if no leave to defend
summary_suit.punjab_specific_notes: Common for recovery of money on bills of exchange, hundis, promissory notes

injunction_suit.court_fees_formula: Fixed court fee of ₹50-100 plus ad valorem if property involved
injunction_suit.limitation_calculation: From date of first infringement or threat
steps: Court hears ex-parte or after notice
If temporary injunction granted, status quo maintained
injunction_suit.punjab_specific_notes: District courts have jurisdiction up to ₹20 lakhs. Higher value goes to civil judge senior division.
